scorecard.note: Provide verifiable sources for the statistics and design clearer, phone‑friendly visuals that directly illustrate each beat.

storyboard.ears: The scariest danger at airports isn't in the sky, it's on the ground.
Serious runway near-misses have more than doubled in about a decade, to 23 last year. That's roughly one every two weeks.
storyboard.eyes: substance: red warning flags; cause: Data places a red warning flag on the runway edge for every near-miss, walking down the runway
storyboard.evidence: Federal Aviation Administration / U.S. Senate Commerce Committee | Serious (Category A/B) US runway incursions per year | https://www.commerce.senate.gov/services/files/E26C0D2B-B5DE-4AE9-BF55-5D0C54843CB8 | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: Six in ten runway incursions last year were people or vehicles wandering onto the runway by mistake, not planes at all.
storyboard.evidence: Federal Aviation Administration | What caused FY2023's 1,756 US runway incursions | https://www.commerce.senate.gov/services/files/E26C0D2B-B5DE-4AE9-BF55-5D0C54843CB8 | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: Just 8 airports, including Boston and Chicago Midway, hold almost a third of the worst ones. That's where the danger lives.
storyboard.evidence: AVweb analysis of FAA data | Share of the worst US runway incursions at just 8 airports | https://avweb.com/aviation-news/us-runway-incursion-hotspots/ | 2026-11-06

storyboard.ears: More flights, same runways. Every close call puts a planeload of people at risk.
